result.stdout:
gscript im — the IM index/linter (imindex) over the operator's memory PLANES

USAGE:
  gscript im lint   [--hub <path>] [--budget N] [--warn-pct N] [--deep] [--strict] [--verbose]
  gscript im digest [--hub <path>] [--budget N]
  gscript im stack  [--hub <path>]   stash -> declared pull (im.json stackPull) -> pop
  gscript im drop   [--hub <path>]   verify-then-drop the flat-stack stash (derived, I-17)
  gscript im fanout [--hub <path>]   DRY-RUN drain proposals: oldest registered bullets
                                     first, declared targets shown, until the plane lands
                                     at its target (proposes only; the drain is a ceremony)
  gscript im check  [--hub <path>] [--filter S] [--update] [--timeout N]
                                     run the registry's runnable falsifiers; scoreboard
                                     PASS/FAIL/SKIP/UNCHECKED; --update stamps lastVerified
  gscript im amend  --bullet NAME --file PATH [--hub <path>]
                                     replace a REGISTERED bullet's extent with the file's
                                     content, lint the full set, keep only on PASS (revert
                                     byte-for-byte on FAIL), stamp + re-anchor the registry

WIDTH (3.0.9): lint measures per-bullet character mass — bulletWarn (default 600,
per-plane in im.json) warns with a count + the widest offender; bulletCap is
ERROR-severity and OFF unless declared. Width is the dimension a line budget
cannot see: drained bullets regrow WIDE before they regrow TALL.

REGISTRY: <hubDir>\falsifiers.json — operator data, private by construction (same law
as im.json). entries[]: { bullet, plane, anchor, target, falsifier, owner,
lastVerified, lastSubstantive, runnable }. fanout sorts by lastSubstantive (content
age — oldest first; falls back to lastVerified) and warns on anchors that no longer
match — the registry is a claim about the hub; drift is a finding.
check's verdict vocabulary is the command's own exit code: timeout/launcher failure is
[truncated]
